samples.question: The picture shows eight solid coloured bars standing side by side on one black baseline: one red, one green, one blue, one orange, one purple, one brown, one pink and one cyan. Every bar has the same width and the bars are evenly spaced, so the bars differ only in HEIGHT. The grey lines above the bars are a knockout bracket and they show only who meets whom. Reading the bars from left to right, the 1st and the 2nd bar are the first match, the 3rd and the 4th the second match, the 5th and the 6th the third and the 7th and the 8th the fourth. ROUND ONE: in each of those four matches the TALLER bar goes through. ROUND TWO: the four bars that went through keep their left-to-right order and meet in two matches, the 1st against the 2nd and the 3rd against the 4th, and now the SHORTER bar goes through. FINAL: the two bars that are left meet and the TALLER of them wins. The answer is the colour of the bar that wins the final. Because the rule alternates, the winner is never the tallest bar in the picture and never the shortest one; in every picture it is also never the second tallest, never the second shortest, and never the bar that would win if the two rules were exchanged so that the shorter bar went through in round one, the taller in round two and the shorter in the final. No two bars that meet in a match are within fifteen pixels of each other in height. Colour is handed out to the eight positions at random and means nothing, and the amount of coloured ink, how far left or right a bar stands and which bars a bar stands beside mean nothing beyond fixing the matches above. Nothing marks the winner: the bracket lines, the pale grey horizontal rules, the dark frame and the black baseline are decoration. Which colour wins the final? Answer red, green, blue, orange, purple, brown, pink or cyan.
